# comment: Copy under the host's local worker-config per project (e.g. local/worker-config/<project>/integration_config.json) and edit paths/commands for that repo. All paths must be absolute. See workforce/integrator.py for field meaning.
# activation_mode: "in_pass" (default) calls activate_cmd inline, verifies, and treats a nonzero rc as activate_failed (stop + park). Use "handoff" only when activate_cmd restarts the daemon the integrator pass itself runs under (e.g. WorkForce activating WorkForce, wf-276): activate_cmd is still called every pass — it must itself never restart from inside the pass, and must instead leave its own durable marker for a scheduled job outside any pass to consume, restarting only once no implementation lane is in flight (production: local/bin/wf-activate.sh writes <version>.pending under local_root/state/integrator-activate/ and exits nonzero; local/bin/wf-activator.sh, run outside the daemon, restarts from that marker). A nonzero rc in handoff mode is never activate_failed: the first time, the pass records outcome activation_handoff and its own bookkeeping marker at local_root/state/integrator-activate/<task-id>.json (task_id, version, release_root, requested_at); later passes with rc still nonzero retry as activation_pending, never stop/park. Once activate_cmd reports rc 0 it has, per its own contract, already removed the external .pending marker, so if verify_cmd then confirms the version the pass clears its own marker and closes — but if verify_cmd still disagrees there is no restart signal left anywhere to wait on, so that case stops and parks for a person exactly like in_pass's verify gate, instead of retrying activation_pending forever. The --clear-recovery CLI flow clears both the bookkeeping marker and the external <version>.pending file (looked up from the marker before it is removed), so a reset order cannot leave the external activator a stale restart request.
notes: Dry run first: python -m workforce integrate --config <this file> --dry-run
Schedulable via cron or the daemon's job scheduling; also runnable manually.
